These come up often in Dr. Mohit’s clinic. Ask him about any others.
“X-rays alone decide if I need surgery.”
Fact: The decision depends on your pain, how much it limits daily life, and how you respond to other treatment, not just on the X-ray.
“Joint replacement is only for very old people.”
Fact: Age matters less than the damage to the joint and your overall health. Some younger people with severe arthritis also benefit.
“After a fracture, rest is all you need.”
Fact: Some fractures need to be set or fixed to heal straight. Long bed rest in older people can also cause stiffness and other problems, so get it checked early.
“Back pain always means a slip disc.”
Fact: Most back pain comes from muscles, joints or posture and improves with exercise and time. A doctor can tell when a scan is actually needed.
“Oil massage will fix a torn ligament.”
Fact: Massage can ease sore muscles but cannot join a torn ligament. A knee that keeps giving way should be examined.

robotic-knee.en: Home
Orthopaedics
Robotic knee
Robotic-assisted knee replacement.
Gupta Hospital uses the Johnson & Johnson VELYS™ robotic-assisted solution. It helps the surgeon plan the operation around your own knee and carry out that plan accurately.
The process
Five steps, start to finish
Assessment
Dr. Mohit examines your knee, reads your X-rays and tells you plainly whether you need surgery, or whether medicines and physiotherapy should come first.
Mapping your knee
During surgery the system records the shape and alignment of your bones, without a separate CT scan beforehand.
Balancing the ligaments
A camera tracks the knee as it bends and straightens, so the soft tissues can be balanced before any bone is cut.
Preparing to plan
A robotic handpiece holds the saw to the planned angle while the surgeon guides it. Only the worn surface is removed.
Recovery
Physiotherapy starts in hospital and continues at home, with follow-up visits at the clinic.
Balancing the knee
Bend the knee and watch the balance.
A camera follows markers on the bones and measures the space on each side of the knee as it bends. Illustration only.

Myths & facts
Common worries, answered
“Do I need a CT scan before robotic surgery?”
No separate CT scan is needed for the VELYS™ system. Your knee is mapped during the operation. You will still need the usual X-rays and blood tests.
“Is robotic surgery right for everyone?”
Not always. Dr. Mohit will look at your knee, your X-rays and your general health, and tell you whether robotic-assisted, conventional or partial replacement suits you best.
“Will I have less pain afterwards?”

Any knee replacement involves some pain while you heal, which is managed with medicines and physiotherapy. Careful soft-tissue handling may help early movement, but recovery differs from person to person.
What is used
Two parts: the system and the implant.
The robotic system helps place the implant. The implant is the new joint surface that stays in your knee.
A camera and a small robotic handpiece that work with the surgeon during the operation.

Cataract surgery is done as day care. Here is roughly how the day goes; your own timings may differ.
Your eye is checked again and drops widen the pupil. Eat a light meal before you come unless told otherwise.
Usually with drops. You stay awake and can talk to the surgeon.
Through a tiny opening, the cloudy lens is removed and a clear lens put in. It often takes under 30 minutes.
You rest with an eye shield while the team checks the eye and explains your drops.
Most people go home in about two hours, with a family member. A check-up is fixed for the next day.
The new lens stays for life.
Before surgery Dr. Parul measures your eye and talks you through the lens options, your daily needs and the cost of each.
Usually set for distance. Most people still use reading glasses.
For people with a cylindrical number, so distance vision is sharper.
Can reduce the need for glasses. Some people notice halos around lights at night.
A folded artificial lens, close up
Fact: No drop or medicine can clear a cataract. Surgery is the only treatment that removes it.
“A cataract must be ripe before surgery.”
Fact: With modern phaco surgery there is no need to wait. Very hard, old cataracts can actually make surgery more difficult.
“My reading got better without glasses, so my eyes are healing.”
Fact: This “second sight” can be an early sign of cataract changing the lens. It is a reason to get an eye check.
“People with diabetes only need eye checks when vision drops.”
Fact: Retina damage from diabetes can start with no symptoms. A yearly retina check is advised.

mental-health.en: Since 2000, Dr. Amit Gupta has worked with families across Malwa facing addiction, depression and anxiety. The hospital runs a licensed de-addiction centre that is clean, quiet and focused on full rehabilitation, with patient confidentiality protected.
You talk, without being rushed. A family member can come with you if you wish.
The doctor explains what may be happening and the treatment options, in plain words.
You agree a plan together. Everything you share stays confidential.
Many people do not know that sleep problems, headaches or memory changes can be treated by a psychiatrist. If something here sounds familiar, it is worth a conversation.
Stress shows up in four places.
Some stress is a normal part of life. When these signs last for weeks, or get in the way of work, family or sleep, talking to a doctor can help.
Will anyone know I came to see a psychiatrist?
No. What you share and your records are kept confidential. Nothing is shared with your employer or relatives without your consent, except where the law requires it.
Will I have to take medicines for life?
Most people do not. Some conditions need only counselling, others need medicines for a set period. Dr. Amit will explain how long and why, and medicines are reduced slowly when it is safe.
Most commonly used medicines, such as antidepressants, are not habit-forming. A few sleep and anxiety medicines can be, so they are used carefully and for short periods.
My family member refuses help. What can I do?
You can come alone first and talk to the doctor about what you are seeing at home. Family sessions can help you find the right way to bring the person in.
Not always. Some people are treated as outpatients. Others need a short stay in the licensed centre while withdrawal is managed safely. The doctor will advise after an assessment.
“Only weak people need mental health care.”
Fact: Mental illness is a health condition, like diabetes or blood pressure. It can affect anyone, and it responds to treatment.
Asking for help is not weakness. What you share with Dr. Amit stays private.
If you need urgent help, call 112 for emergencies or the national Tele-MANAS helpline on 14416, any time.

about.en: In 1980 Dr. Amrit Gupta opened a small orthopaedic clinic on Power House Road so that people in and around Bathinda would not have to travel to big cities for bone and joint surgery. The hospital still works by that idea: specialist care, close to home, at a fair cost.
Today his children lead the three departments, and each of them still sees patients personally.
